title: Man killed in Vancouver gas station shootout known to police
article: The man shot and killed by a veteran cop at a gas station in Vancouver's east side Monday afternoon was known to police, a spokesman said Wednesday.
Const. Tim Fanning said Reuben Coleman, 21, had no fixed address and was believed to have spent a lot of time in Abbotsford, B.C.
Police didn't disclose further information about the shootout, except that an autopsy has been conducted and toxicology results won't be available for six weeks.
Coleman was shot at the Shell gas station at the corner of E41st Avenue and Knight Street after police received a report of an impaired driver.

CBC News has learned the officer who fatally shot Coleman is Const. Randy Bell, who has served the Vancouver Police Department for 17 years and is described as a solid and reputable police officer. He is not currently on active duty.
Bell was named Police Officer of the Year in 1993.

Police said on Tuesday a lone police officer arrived in an unmarked police vehicle and found a man near the gas pumps changing a damaged tire on his car. The officer wound up in a struggle with the man.

"During the struggle the suspect, who had a gun, fired a number of shots. The officer was able to pull away from the suspect. More shots were fired. The suspect was hit by a round and he later died from his injuries," Fanning said Tuesday.
